- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean or dip magnitude.
- Model consistently under-responds to sentiment shifts; lag correction: if sentiment turns positive after 2–3 days, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- After sharp price spikes (≥ 5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots in next 3–7 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use moving average smoothing.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 3–5% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 0.5–1.0% per day.
- Sentiment + price divergence: if sentiment > 0.67 but price is flat or falling, model underestimates upside; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 5 days.
- Sentiment + price convergence: if sentiment < 0.33 but price is rising, model overestimates upside; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 5 days.
